method_note: Public web research only (WebSearch + WebFetch/curl on public pages). No logins bypassed, no bot-walls circumvented. Deliberately did NOT re-scrape the three sources already in hand (basketball.qc.ca 'réseau basketball Québec' regional pages, the regional PDF registries, and the clubs_et_organisations page) beyond spot-checking that they still resolve. All new club names below were surfaced via the angles in the brief: MBL full roster, Circuit/Ligue Basketball Québec, Quebec Youth Basketball League, municipal/loisirs directories for named zero-club municipalities, and French-language private-academy searches.

directories.notes: Already in hand per brief (~56 clubs) — not re-scraped in depth. Confirmed the region URLs still resolve (HTTP 200) and are static HTML (no JS map). The standalone 'ou_jouer.html' page cited in the brief now 404s; the live entry point is the region list under /fr/page/organisation_clubassociation.html. No Google My Maps iframe found anywhere on basketball.qc.ca — checked ou_jouer.html, organisation_clubassociation.html, and the Montréal regional page's raw HTML for 'google.com/maps/d/'; none present. Basketball Québec does not appear to run an interactive map.

directories.name: Circuit Basketball Québec (CBQ) — kreezee-sports.com platform
directories.notes: AngularJS single-page app — team/organization data loads via an internal API that could not be discovered from the static bundle (no public REST endpoint found; /api/teams and /api/organizations both 404). Front page and /equipes, /classement routes return only an empty app shell via curl/WebFetch. WORKAROUND: individual team pages ARE indexed by search engines with real titles (Google cache), so 'site:circuit-basketball-quebec.kreezee-sports.com' searches surfaced team names: CB Drummondville, Escadron Sport-Études, É.S Henri-Bourassa, Noir et Or É.S. De Mortagne, Fondation Fusion Élite, Vortex É.S.Gérard-Fillion, Pionniers É.S. Polybel, Géants Polyvalente St-Jérôme, DV Élite (school-tied, likely École secondaire Dalbé-Viau), Collège NDL, Club de Basketball les Astéries, École secondaire Dalbé-Viau, Association régionale de basketball Laval. Basketball Québec states the CBQ has 57 organizations / 220+ teams province-wide (2025-2026), but only this Montréal/Laurentides-heavy subset is search-indexed — the rest (including any Québec City, Sherbrooke, Gatineau, Saguenay entries) could not be enumerated without a login or API access. All named teams here map to clubs/schools already in the census.

directories.name: MaCommunaute.ca / arrondissement.com — Quebec community-organization directory (bottin des organismes)
directories.notes: Broad province-wide 'bottin' covering Montréal boroughs, Laval, and beyond (arrondissement.com now 301-redirects into this same platform). Useful as a cross-check but its on-site search (?s=, ?mc_search=) does not actually filter — confirmed by identical irrelevant result sets across three different param names. Had to rely on Google's 'site:' search instead, which surfaced: Club de Basket-Ball de Saint-Léonard, Basket-Ball Les Lynx de St-Hubert, Ligue de basketball extérieure de l'Ouest-de-l'Île (=WIOBL), Association régionale de basketball de Laval, Association de basketball West Island Lakers (=WILBA), Fédération de basketball du Québec, Association de basketball de Saint-Bruno, DOD-Basketball — all already known. No new clubs surfaced from this source.

directories.name: Zone Loisir Montérégie — member list
directories.notes: Full member directory (Classe A/B/C + associate, ~200 orgs across Montérégie) fetched in full. Only one basketball entry: 'Club de basketball Les Tornades' (Longueuil, already known). Confirms Montérégie's municipal recreation network does not itself run basketball programs beyond the handful of clubs already in the census — most Montérégie towns route kids through regional clubs (Tornades, CBO/Cavaliers, DBC) rather than town-run programs.

coverage_assessment: The 169-club Quebec census is still a significant undercount, but the shortfall is concentrated in a specific place: private/independent academies and hyper-local town programs that never touch a federation registry, not in undiscovered regional associations. This sweep confirmed the federation layer (Basketball Québec regional pages, CBQ, LBQ) is largely already captured — the JS-rendered kreezee-sports.com platform behind CBQ/LBQ hides its full 57-organization/220-team roster behind an app shell with no public API, and the slice recoverable via search-engine indexing maps almost entirely onto clubs the census already has. The one genuinely new competitive layer found is QYBL/LJBQ (qybl.ca), an independent Montréal/Rive-Sud youth league outside the Basketball Québec/MBL/CBQ family entirely — its 13-team roster added several new names (Sonic de St-Amable, AGBU, plus low-confidence Wexl/Ace Warriors/DD Basketball that could not be corroborated elsewhere). Municipal-directory scraping (the angle expected to be highest-yield) mostly proved that the five named zero-club municipalities are REAL gaps, not research gaps: Mirabel and Salaberry-de-Valleyfield have no dedicated youth basketball club at all (confirmed via their own sports-club directories), Vaudreuil-Dorion is served by the already-known CBO/Cavaliers rather than its own club, and only Rouyn-Noranda yielded a genuine new find (Basketball Rouyn-Noranda). This suggests the true province-wide club count is probably in the 200-260 range rather than dramatically higher than 169 — Quebec's basketball infrastructure appears to be real but thin outside Greater Montréal/Laval/Longueuil, unlike Ontario where the gap was concentrated in one undiscovered provincial registry. The remaining undercount likely lives in three places this sweep could only partially reach: (1) each Centre de services scolaire's own 'mandataire sportif' list for sport-études programs (the one document found was 404; there are ~72 CSS/CSSP boards province-wide, each potentially naming 1-3 basketball mandataires), (2) small single-city private academies with no social presence beyond Instagram (weak signal, hard to search), and (3) the un-indexed remainder of the CBQ/LBQ team rosters. Regions with almost no independent verification in this sweep, positive or negative: Bas-Saint-Laurent (beyond Rimouski, already known), Gaspésie–Îles-de-la-Madeleine, Côte-Nord beyond Baie-Comeau, and most of Abitibi-Témiscamingue beyond Rouyn-Noranda — these were searched but returned only CEGEP/school programs, not community clubs, which may reflect either a real absence of organized youth basketball or simply weak web presence in low-population regions.
next_best_sources: Enumerate each of Quebec's ~72 Centres de services scolaires' own 'programme sport-études / concentration basketball / club mandataire' pages individually — Basketball Québec's own 'Liste des programmes Sport-études et Concentration' page (basketball.qc.ca/fr/page/programme_dexcellence/liste_des_programmes_sport-etudes_et_concentration.html) is a ready-made index of these and was NOT deep-scraped in this pass — likely the single highest-yield remaining source for private-academy discovery.

Reverse-engineer or request API access to the kreezee-sports.com backend behind circuit-basketball-quebec and ligue-basketball-quebec — the full 57-org/220-team CBQ roster and full LBQ roster exist server-side but are invisible to a public scrape; a logged-in account or a request to Basketball Québec (contact: ymercier@basketball.qc.ca) for the CSV/PDF team list would close this gap directly.

QYBL (qybl.ca, info@qybl.ca) — contact directly for their full multi-season team history; this sweep only saw the current Autumn 2026/Winter 2027 roster and could not corroborate 3 of 13 team names (Wexl, Ace Warriors, DD Basketball) elsewhere.

Facebook Graph/Page search for Quebec cities + 'basketball' + 'club'/'académie' with a logged-in account — repeatedly hit real-looking leads (Vaudreuil Basketball, Club de basketball de Beauce) that a login-free sweep could not verify or extract contact details from.

Instagram hashtag/location search for smaller regions (Bas-Saint-Laurent, Gaspésie, Côte-Nord, most of Abitibi) — private academies in low-population regions appear to have Instagram-only presence with no indexed website, which this sweep's search-engine-based method is structurally weak against.

Direct outreach to the 15 regional 'unités régionales de loisir et de sport' offices (contacts already in qc-pdf-clubs.json) asking specifically for basketball-club rosters — these bodies administer regional sport development and would know of clubs with no web presence at all.
